overview: Spicy's Reach overrides the client's block-reach distance through the EventGetBlockReach hook. The module exposes a NumberSetting named Reach (default 3, minimum 3, maximum 6, step 0.1), updates the HUD description on EventUpdate, and on EventGetBlockReach cancels the event and sets event.reach to the configured value. The patched PlayerControllerMP.getBlockReachDistance constructs the event, fires it, and returns event.reach whenever it is not -1, falling back to the vanilla 5.0 creative or 4.5 survival distance otherwise. In 1.8 the mouse-over ray trace that decides both block interaction and entity attack targets uses this distance as its cap, so raising it extends entity attack reach up to 6 blocks; a vanilla server performs no reach validation of its own, which is exactly why anticheats must.

sections.p: The fork's PlayerControllerMP.getBlockReachDistance builds an EventGetBlockReach, sets its type to PRE, fires it through SpicyClient.onEvent, and returns event.reach when the field is not -1. The Reach module listens for the event in its pre phase, cancels it, and writes the configured value into the reach field. Cancelling the event prevents later handlers from overriding the value, and the field write is what the vanilla method reads back. The module's onDisable clears the use-item key binding, a leftover unrelated to the reach mechanic itself.

EntityRenderer.getMouseOver ray-traces entities with a distance cap equal to the block-reach distance, and PlayerControllerMP.attackEntity acts on the mouse-over result without any additional distance validation, so getBlockReachDistance is effectively the player's attack range. The vanilla 1.8 server does not check how far an attack reaches; the only server-side limit is the coarse bound on entity hits. Raising the client distance to 6 therefore makes C02 attacks land on targets the real 3.0 to 4.5 block envelope would never cover, with the server none the wiser. The same cap governs block interaction, so the module also extends placement and breaking ranges, though the analysis focuses on the combat consequence.

The setting spans 3 to 6 in 0.1 steps with a default of 3, which is the vanilla survival value, so the module is a no-op until the user raises it. The HUD description echoes the current value on every EventUpdate, which makes the active range visible in the client's own module list. The distance is applied globally, with no per-target or per-tick randomization, so the module presents a constant extended range that server-side reach checks can measure on every single attack.

files.label: Reach.java (module)
files.explanation: The module is the Reach NumberSetting plus two handlers. The EventUpdate pre handler updates the HUD text with the current value, and the EventGetBlockReach handler cancels the event and writes the value into event.reach. The constructor registers the setting with the 3 to 6 range and 0.1 step, and resetSettings re-registers it on reset. onDisable clears the use-item binding, which does not participate in the reach mechanic. The module never sends a packet; its entire effect is the value the patched vanilla method reads.

files.label: PlayerControllerMP.java (reach integration)
files.explanation: The patched getBlockReachDistance is the integration point that makes the setting effective. It constructs EventGetBlockReach with the PRE type, dispatches it through SpicyClient.onEvent, and returns event.reach when the field differs from -1, otherwise the vanilla 5.0 creative or 4.5 survival distance. Every call site of getBlockReachDistance, most importantly the EntityRenderer mouse-over ray trace, then sees the module's value, which is how a reach of 6 becomes the attack range without any change to the attack code itself. The file also shows the fork's general event dispatch pattern used by the other combat modules.

countering.label: Reach (eye-to-box distance)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus measures the eye-to-target distance for every attack against the survival distance limit, default 4.02, subtracting a getinset half-width when reachPrecision is on. A Spicy reach of 4.5 to 6 presents a measured distance well past the limit on every hit, so the violation fires on the first attack and the reachMod mechanism compounds it: repeated hits near the band step the modifier down and silently cancel borderline attacks even below the nominal ceiling. The check also feeds Improbable with the excess distance, so sustained extended reach accumulates on a second layer. Because the module applies the range constantly with no oscillation, there is no window of compliant attacks to reset the decay.

countering.label: FightHitbox (lag-compensated ray trace)
countering.explanation: Hawk re-runs the hit on the server against the victim's real hitbox. It stores the InteractEntityEvent, waits for the next MoveEvent because 1.8 sends the attack before the yaw update, builds the ray from the eye position and the move's yaw and pitch, rewinds the victim to the lag-compensated position, and intersects against the standard 0.6-wide box expanded by only 0.005. The intersect distance is compared with maxReach 3.1, plus 1.9 in creative. A 4.5 to 6 block attack either misses the box entirely, earning the Did not hit hitbox. punishment, or intersects at a distance well past 3.1, earning a reach punish. The module's constant extended range means every sampled attack fails one of the two branches.

countering.label: Reach (packet-entity ray trace)
countering.explanation: Grim queues each attack position and performs the precise ray trace on the next look update against the packet-entity box rebuilt from server teleport and rel-move data, checking all possible look directions and eye heights to cover the one-tick look lag, with a 0.1 hitbox margin for pre-1.9 clients. The trace is bounded by the server-side reach, so a 6-block Spicy attack is rejected with the intersection failing beyond the box or the distance exceeding the threshold, and the cancelBuffer then suppresses the next several attacks, which stops a killaura or autoclicker feeding hits into the extended range. The margin covers genuine knockback and lag on borderline hits, not a constant 6-block envelope.

countering.label: KillAura (reach sub-check)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's reach sub-check computes the distance between the player and the victim's location minus the victim's current velocity, so knockback does not inflate the measurement, and compares it with max-reach 4.2 from config.yml. The client-side reach value is invisible to this math: the check measures actual server positions, and a hit at 4.5 to 6 blocks from the center exceeds 4.2 on every attack, regardless of what the client believed its range was. Because the module applies a constant range, the violation is deterministic, and the cancel action at cancel-vl 0 reverts the attacker to their original location, which both punishes the extended hit and resets the fight geometry.
